wi_central_sandstone.blurb: Central Sandstone is a scattering of sandstone bluffs and boulders rising out of the flat central plains of Adams County, Wisconsin, between Adams-Friendship and Wisconsin Dells. Bouldering is the most common style, mixed with trad, top-rope and some sport. Rattlesnake Mound is a large bluff line with sandstone boulders strewn along it, and Shiprock is a small roadside bluff of soft sandstone with sport, trad and top-rope lines. Owens Rock and Quincy Bluff add smaller helpings. Boulder problems run from V0 into the upper grades, mostly V0 to V5, while roped routes span 5.4 to 5.12 and cluster around 5.10 and below. At Shiprock the rock is soft and still shedding loose pieces.

wy_guernsey_state_park.blurb: Guernsey State Park lies on the North Platte River near the town of Guernsey in southeast Wyoming, with climbing spread over several canyon walls. It is almost entirely sport climbing, with 5.10 and 5.11 the bulk of the routes, a few easier ones from 5.6 and a smaller group at 5.12. The Red and White Grotto Walls hold by far the most routes, followed by Dead Man's Gulch. Rock quality varies a great deal: the red rock at the Grotto Walls is iron-stained quartzite capped by gray dolomite, with pockets, steep faces and roofs, and there is loose, fractured rock to watch for. South-facing walls can be among the warmest winter spots in Wyoming but are best skipped in summer, apart from early mornings.

ca_06_little_lakes_valley_mono_recesses.blurb: Little Lakes Valley and the Mono Recesses form a high-elevation stretch of the High Sierra reached from Highway 395 near Toms Place. Little Lakes Valley is an open landscape of meadows, streams and widely exposed granite, with more than a dozen small lakes and five summits above 13,000 feet. The Mono Recesses are hanging valleys west of Mono Pass. Climbing is a blend: alpine and trad routes on peaks and ridges such as Bear Creek Spire and Ruby Peak, with a few scrambles and ice lines, plus a large share of bouldering at Morgan Pass, mostly V0 to V4. The valley's trail is usually open from early summer to early fall.

ca_crafts_peak.blurb: Crafts Peak is a climbing area on the southwestern flanks of Crafts Peak in the San Bernardino Mountains, near Green Valley Lake, at around 7,800 feet. The crags sit on a steep, forested ridge with views toward Lake Arrowhead, the San Gabriel Mountains and the desert, and part of the forest was burned in a 2007 fire. Climbing is mostly trad on pinnacles and large blocks, with some proper cragging, a few sport lines and some top-ropes. Routes are mostly short, around 20 to 40 feet, with grades from the lowest 5th class to 5.11 and the bulk between 5.7 and 5.10. Rock quality is inconsistent, from clean and nearly polished to grainy and lichen-covered, sometimes on different faces of one formation. The ridge splits into a north side and a south side.

ca_lizard_s_mouth_the.blurb: The Lizard's Mouth is a bouldering area on the ridge of the Santa Ynez Mountains above Santa Barbara, with Pacific views toward the Channel Islands. The rock is sandstone, from large boulders to a massive overhanging formation, and the problems are split among many small groups of boulders, including Femme Fatale Area, Top of the World, Sunset Boulevard and Meilee Area. A cave with a long traverse is a main attraction, with many harder problems inside it. Nearly all of the climbing is bouldering, with easier problems dominating: most fall between V0 and V3, and a thinner run goes up to V8. A few top-rope lines also exist.
